verdict.rationale: Adyen documents outbound webhooks that deliver asynchronous status changes, so you need not poll. It also keeps a Customer Area log of all webhook events sent to your server, and its Management API tooling can list, get, and test webhooks. However, the evidence never mentions signed deliveries (e.g. HMAC), automatic retry behavior, or event replay, which are core parts of this story. missing for 10: signed webhook payload verification, automatic retry policy, event replay/resend capability, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can rely on signed webhook deliveries with automatic retries, event logs, and replay to keep my system consistent with payment state

citations.quote: With webhooks, you can avoid having to continuously poll an API endpoint, waiting for a change in status for an asynchronous process
In your Customer Area, you can find a log of all webhook events sent to your server.
Adyen sends a webhook message with the payment outcome to your webhook server.
